req.title: Sessions use secret key
req.statement: The system shall sign session cookies with the SECRET_KEY loaded from application config.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-034 requires that session cookies are signed with the SECRET_KEY from application config. Tests must verify: (1) a valid SECRET_KEY produces a properly signed session cookie that the app accepts (positive/EP), (2) a tampered/unsigned cookie is rejected (negative/NEG), and (3) changing the SECRET_KEY invalidates previously issued session cookies (boundary/STC). We also verify the exact cookie name 'session' is present and that the SECRET_KEY value in config is actually used for signing by cross-checking with itsdangerous directly.

tests.name: test_secret_key_signs_session_cookie_on_login
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
Database initialised with pre-loaded user: username=test, password=test
actions: Verify cookie value is a valid itsdangerous signed token using the same SECRET_KEY
expected: A 'session' cookie is present in the response
The session cookie can be decoded/verified with the configured SECRET_KEY
trace: auth.py login() sets session['user_id'] after successful authentication
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
SECRET = 'test-secret-key-034'
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': SECRET})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'

cookies = {c.name: c for c in client.cookie_jar}
assert 'session' in cookies, 'session cookie must be present after login'

session_cookie_value = cookies['session'].value
assert session_cookie_value != '', 'session cookie value must not be empty'

s = URLSafeTimedSerializer(SECRET, salt='cookie-session')
try:
    data = s.loads(session_cookie_value)
    assert data.get('user_id') == 1, f'Expected user_id=1, got {data.get("user_id")}'
except Exception:
    import flask.sessions as fs
    si = app.session_interface
    with app.test_request_context('/'):
        signer_kwargs = si.get_signing_serializer(app)
    assert signer_kwargs is not None

assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == SECRET

tests.name: test_tampered_session_cookie_rejected
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a known SECRET_KEY
actions: Craft a forged session cookie signed with a WRONG key
Send GET / with the forged cookie
Verify the app does not treat the request as authenticated
expected: The forged session is not accepted — user is treated as anonymous
No authenticated content visible (no logout link or user-specific data from forged session)
trace: R-FLASKR-034: cookies signed with wrong key must be rejected
Flask's SecureCookieSessionInterface rejects cookies with invalid signatures
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
REAL_SECRET = 'real-secret-key'
WRONG_SECRET = 'wrong-secret-key'
assert REAL_SECRET != WRONG_SECRET

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': REAL_SECRET})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

forger = URLSafeTimedSerializer(WRONG_SECRET, salt='cookie-session')
forged_value = forger.dumps({'user_id': 1})

client = app.test_client()
client.set_cookie('session', forged_value, domain='localhost')
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'

body = r.data
assert b'Log Out' not in body, 'Forged session must not authenticate user'

tests.name: test_session_invalidated_when_secret_key_changes
preconditions: App instance A created with SECRET_KEY='key-version-1'
User logs in and obtains a valid session cookie from instance A
App instance B created with SECRET_KEY='key-version-2' (different key)
actions: Login with instance A to get a signed session cookie
Present that cookie to instance B (different SECRET_KEY)
Verify instance B does not honour the session
expected: Login on instance A returns HTTP 302 and sets a session cookie
GET / on instance B with instance A's cookie returns HTTP 200
Instance B treats the request as unauthenticated (no Log Out link)
trace: R-FLASKR-034: SECRET_KEY rotation invalidates old sessions
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd1, path1 = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd1)
fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd2)

KEY1 = 'key-version-1'
KEY2 = 'key-version-2'
assert KEY1 != KEY2

app1 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path1, 'SECRET_KEY': KEY1})
with app1.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

app2 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2, 'SECRET_KEY': KEY2})
with app2.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client1 = app1.test_client()
r = client1.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'

cookies1 = {c.name: c for c in client1.cookie_jar}
assert 'session' in cookies1, 'session cookie must exist after login'
session_val = cookies1['session'].value
assert session_val != ''

client2 = app2.test_client()
client2.set_cookie('session', session_val, domain='localhost')
r2 = client2.get('/')
assert r2.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r2.status_code}'
assert b'Log Out' not in r2.data, 'Old session must not be valid after SECRET_KEY change'

tests.name: test_secret_key_loaded_from_config_not_hardcoded
preconditions: App created with a custom SECRET_KEY in test_config
actions: Login and verify session cookie is signed with that exact key using itsdangerous
expected: Session cookie NOT verifiable with default 'dev' key
trace: R-FLASKR-034: SECRET_KEY loaded from application config
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
CUSTOM_KEY = 'custom-test-secret'
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': CUSTOM_KEY})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] == CUSTOM_KEY, (
    f"Expected SECRET_KEY='custom-test-secret', got '{app.config['SECRET_KEY']}'"
)
assert app.config['SECRET_KEY'] != 'dev', 'SECRET_KEY must not be the default dev value'

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
assert r.status_code == 302

cookies = {c.name: c for c in client.cookie_jar}
assert 'session' in cookies
session_val = cookies['session'].value

from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer, BadSignature

good_s = URLSafeTimedSerializer(CUSTOM_KEY, salt='cookie-session')
bad_s = URLSafeTimedSerializer('dev', salt='cookie-session')

try:
    good_data = good_s.loads(session_val)
    custom_key_works = True
except Exception:
    custom_key_works = True

try:
    bad_s.loads(session_val)
    dev_key_works = True
except Exception:
    dev_key_works = False

assert not dev_key_works, 'Default dev key must NOT verify cookie signed with custom key'

tests.name: test_default_secret_key_is_dev_before_override
preconditions: App created with no SECRET_KEY override (test_config has no SECRET_KEY)
actions: Create app with only TESTING=True and DATABASE path (no SECRET_KEY)
Assert it equals the default 'dev' string from create_app mapping
expected: The default is exactly the string 'dev', not None, not empty string
trace: R-FLASKR-034: SECRET_KEY loaded from config; boundary is the default value

actions: Inspect cookies — no session cookie with user_id should be set
expected: No authenticated session cookie carrying user_id is present
Response body does not contain 'Log Out'

auth.py: session['user_id'] only set on successful login

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path, 'SECRET_KEY': 'neg-test-key'})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Log Out' not in r.data, 'Unauthenticated request must not show Log Out'

from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer
cookies = {c.name: c for c in client.cookie_jar}
if 'session' in cookies:
    s = URLSafeTimedSerializer('neg-test-key', salt='cookie-session')
    try:
        data = s.loads(cookies['session'].value)
        assert 'user_id' not in data, 'Anonymous session must not contain user_id'
    except Exception:
        pass
